Commodity Supercycle? Some analysts are predicting a new commodity supercycle driven by the energy transition. The demand for lithium, copper, cobalt, and rare earth metals could increase 4-6x by 2035, according to the IEA. "The clean energy transition is the most resource-intensive transition in human history," says commodities investor Dr. Goehring. "You can't build millions of electric vehicles and solar panels without mining the materials. The demand is real; the question is whether supply can keep up."

Once you have the foundation, you can experiment with more advanced approaches. For individual investors, the rise of ESG Investing raises practical questions about portfolio construction, risk management, and time horizon. Conventional advice was built for a different era, and some of it no longer applies cleanly. But the core principles — diversification, cost control, discipline — remain as relevant as ever. The challenge is applying those principles to a rapidly changing environment.

"The programs exist; engagement doesn't," says workplace benefits consultant Jennifer Marks. "The companies seeing results are those that integrate financial wellness into the flow of work — payroll integration, benefits enrollment nudges, and paycheck-time savings prompts."

Interest Rate Strategy: A study by Vanguard found that investors who stayed fully invested during the 2022-2024 rate hiking cycle performed better than those who tried to time the market — by an average of 4.5% annually. "The temptation to go to cash when rates rise is strong," says Vanguard senior economist Roger Aliaga-Diaz. "But history consistently shows that staying the course wins. The pain of staying invested is temporary; the cost of missing the recovery is permanent."
